overall_summary: Bitcoin is holding near sixty-five thousand as the market waits on today's jobs report for direction. Whale accumulation and steady ETF inflows provide a supportive bid underneath, while the Clarity Act delay and firmer oil from Gulf tensions keep some caution in play. Soft private payrolls hint at cooling labor conditions that could ease rate pressure if confirmed.
key_points: Senate delays Clarity Act until after recess
Soft ADP print flags cooling private hiring
NFP jobs data is today's key catalyst
Oil firm on Hormuz and Gulf tensions

items.title: Senate Delays Clarity Act Vote Until After August Recess
items.summary: The U.S. Senate will not vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before its summer break, pushing any action to mid-September at the earliest. Majority Leader Thune confirmed no August vote amid unresolved issues including ethics provisions tied to Trump crypto holdings and Democratic opposition. Traders should care because this major market-structure bill is seen as a key unlock for broader institutional participation, and the delay removes a near-term positive catalyst while raising questions about full-year passage odds.
items.impact: Removes near-term regulatory tailwind and pressures sentiment on majors

items.title: Bitcoin Whales Accumulate $1.2 Billion as ETFs Take $750 Million
items.summary: Wallets holding 10 to 10,000 BTC added over 20,000 bitcoin worth about $1.2 billion since late July while price chopped below 65,000. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in roughly 755 million dollars this week, on pace for the strongest week since April, led by BlackRock's IBIT. Traders should watch this because large holders and institutions are buying the range even as retail stays cautious after the Coldcard mess, providing a potential floor if price can finally close decisively above 65k.
items.impact: Builds accumulation base and cushions downside near key levels

items.title: Coldcard Fallout: 210,000 BTC Exit Long-Term Holder Wallets
items.summary: Glassnode data shows roughly 210,000 bitcoin left long-term holder supply over the past week, the biggest drop since late 2024, dropping the cohort from nearly 15 million to about 14.7 million BTC. This is linked to the ongoing Coldcard hardware wallet exploit that drained up to around 130 million dollars, with users rushing to new wallets or regulated custody rather than dumping into the market. Traders should care because the move looks like a custody migration, not distribution, and it has coincided with ETF inflows as some shift away from pure self-custody risk.
items.impact: Heightens custody concerns but supports ETF demand without heavy selling pressure

items.title: Bitcoin Hovers Near $65K Ahead of Jobs Data Amid Oil Spike
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around 64,300 to 65,000 heading into Friday's U.S. nonfarm payrolls report, little changed on the week, as Brent crude jumped on stalled Hormuz talks and Middle East tensions. Higher oil revives inflation fears that keep yields elevated and the Fed leaning hawkish, capping risk assets. Traders need to watch the jobs print closely because a soft number could reopen rate-cut hopes and let BTC break its summer range, while a strong one stacked on oil strength would reinforce the ceiling near 65k.
items.impact: Macro event risk; resolution of range depends on data and yields reaction

items.title: Wintermute Secures SEC Broker-Dealer Status for Equities and ETFs
items.summary: Crypto market maker Wintermute's U.S. arm registered with the SEC and joined FINRA as a broker-dealer, allowing it to trade U.S. stocks and options, provide ETF liquidity as an authorized participant, and self-clear digital asset securities for proprietary accounts. The firm already handles over 10 billion in daily volume and plans to focus on crypto-linked products while eyeing tokenized stocks later. This matters for traders as another bridge between crypto liquidity providers and traditional Wall Street rails, potentially improving ETF creation-redemption efficiency and institutional access.
items.impact: Advances crypto-TradFi integration and ETF market plumbing

items.title: 2011 Dormant Bitcoin Wallet Moves $3.2 Million Toward FalconX
items.summary: A wallet that received nearly 50 BTC in 2011 when bitcoin was around 10 dollars awakened and transferred about 3.2 million dollars worth to a SegWit address previously linked to FalconX deposits and other institutional flows. The coins sat unmoved for 15 years and have not yet left the new address. In the current Coldcard-driven climate of long-term holders reviewing old setups, such moves draw attention as possible signs of reorganization or preparation for liquidity, though no sale is confirmed yet.
items.impact: Highlights old-supply mobility; limited immediate price effect unless sold

items.title: July NFP Jobs Report Drops Today Amid Fed Hike Watch
items.summary: The big one lands this morning. Markets expect the US to have added around 80 to 83 thousand nonfarm payrolls in July, a modest rebound from June's soft 57 thousand, with unemployment steady at 4.2 percent and wages up 0.3 percent month over month. This is the last major labor reading before the September FOMC, where traders see roughly even odds of a rate hike after the divided July hold at 3.5 to 3.75 percent. Crypto traders should care because a big miss could kill hike bets and boost risk assets, while a hot print would firm the dollar and yields and pressure Bitcoin.
items.impact: High volatility catalyst for USD, yields, and risk assets including crypto

items.title: Jobless Claims Edge to 199k, Layoffs Hit Two-Year Low
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims rose just one thousand to 199 thousand in the week ending August 1, coming in below the 202 thousand forecast and staying near multi-decade lows. Separate data showed planned layoffs plunged 27 percent in July to a two-year low of about 33 thousand. This paints a picture of a still-resilient but not overheating labor market heading into the full jobs report. For traders it supports the idea that the Fed can stay patient on rates unless inflation reaccelerates, which is mildly supportive for risk assets if it keeps hike odds in check.
items.impact: Supports stable labor narrative, limited immediate market move

items.title: Treasury Yields Steady Near 4.66% Ahead of Payrolls
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield held around 4.66 to 4.67 percent on Friday morning with little movement, while the 2-year sat near 4.23 percent and the 30-year near 5.21 percent. Yields have eased slightly in recent sessions as markets digest soft private payrolls and await confirmation from the official jobs data. Bond traders are pricing the path of Fed policy, and any surprise in today's report will quickly reprice the curve. Crypto cares because falling yields and a softer dollar typically ease financial conditions and favor Bitcoin, while a yield spike does the opposite.
items.impact: Sets the tone for rate expectations; NFP will drive the next leg

items.title: Dollar Index Hovers Near 100 Ahead of Key Jobs Data
items.summary: The US Dollar Index is trading just under 100, around 99.9, after recent softness that brought it close to multi-week lows. It has been range-bound as traders balance geopolitical oil risks against cooling labor signals and mixed Fed signals. A strong NFP would likely lift the greenback and weigh on gold and crypto, while a miss could extend dollar weakness. For crypto traders the dollar's direction remains a core inverse driver of Bitcoin prices in the short term.
items.impact: NFP-driven move in DXY will spill into crypto risk appetite

items.title: Soft ADP Print of 44k Flags Cooling Private Hiring
items.summary: Private payrolls rose only 44 thousand in July according to ADP, well below the 75 thousand expected and down from a revised 95 thousand prior. The miss, released earlier this week, has reinforced concerns that job growth is slowing after stronger spring numbers and raised the stakes for today's official BLS report. Pay growth remained firm, however. This soft private-sector signal leans against aggressive Fed tightening and is being watched closely by markets pricing September odds.
items.impact: Lowers near-term hike odds, supportive for risk assets if confirmed

items.title: ISM Manufacturing Surges to 55.6, Strongest Since 2022
items.summary: Factory activity accelerated sharply in July with the ISM Manufacturing PMI jumping to 55.6 from 53.3, beating forecasts and hitting the highest level since May 2022. Production, new orders, and employment all expanded, with the jobs component returning to growth for the first time in many months. Elevated prices remain a concern but eased slightly. This points to resilient industrial demand helped by AI investment and front-loading, which could keep the Fed focused on inflation even if the labor market cools.
items.impact: Supports growth narrative but keeps inflation vigilance alive

items.title: Saudi, Turkey, Pakistan Sign Mutual Defense Pact
items.summary: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have signed a NATO-style mutual defense agreement in Mecca, treating an attack on one as an attack on all. This comes as the Iran war spills over with threats to Gulf oil infrastructure. Traders should watch because it reshapes Middle East alliances, potentially deterring further proxy attacks or drawing in more players and raising energy risk premiums.
items.impact: Could stabilize Gulf security or heighten bloc tensions, mixed for oil and risk assets

items.title: Houthis Escalate; Saudi Braces for Coordinated Attacks
items.summary: Houthi forces launched attacks killing and wounding dozens near the Yemen-Saudi border, while Saudi officials cite intelligence of imminent multi-pronged strikes by Iranian-backed Iraqi militias and Houthis on ports and airports. This widens the Iran war into a broader regional fight. Crypto traders care because fresh attacks on energy infrastructure keep oil elevated and drive risk-off moves in equities and Bitcoin.
items.impact: Elevates oil prices and geopolitical risk premium, pressuring risk assets

items.title: Iran-Oman Near Hormuz Shipping Deal Amid Ban Push
items.summary: Iran and Oman are finalizing a framework for limited commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, but Iranian lawmakers are drafting rules to bar US and Israeli vessels and the deal would not fully reopen the waterway. Oil prices held recent gains on caution. This matters for markets because any partial reopening could ease the oil shock, while restrictions keep supply tight and volatility high for risk assets.
items.impact: Unresolved deal keeps oil elevated and markets range-bound pending clarity

items.title: Trump Denies US Munitions Shortage in Iran War
items.summary: Reports say the US has burned through most long-range missiles and a large share of Patriot and THAAD interceptors after five months of war with Iran. Trump pushed back hard, claiming massive stocks, hunting leakers, and saying the war could end soon. Traders should note this because depleted stockpiles may limit US options, prolong the conflict, and sustain high oil prices and uncertainty that weigh on risk appetite.
items.impact: Signals potential prolonged conflict and readiness concerns, supporting risk-off

items.title: DRC Bans Copper and Cobalt Concentrate Exports
items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates to force more domestic processing, with limited waivers possible. Copper prices jumped on the news as Congo is a top global supplier of these battery metals. This hits traders because tighter supply of critical minerals can stoke inflation and disrupt EV and tech supply chains, adding another layer of commodity volatility.
items.impact: Supports copper prices short-term; broader inflation and supply-chain risks mixed for markets

items.title: Oil Holds Gains on Hormuz Caution and Gulf Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude steadied near 82 dollars after a nearly 4 percent surge, as markets weighed partial Hormuz progress against Iran's vessel restrictions and widening proxy attacks. The Iran war continues to dominate energy flows. Crypto traders watch oil closely here because sustained high prices feed inflation fears and can pressure risk assets including Bitcoin until a clear de-escalation path emerges.
items.impact: Keeps energy inflation pressure and geopolitical overhang on risk markets
